title: Affine higher-image section functors and canonical Leray normalization
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $A$ a commutative ring, $Y$ a scheme over $S$ with a specified isomorphism $a:Y ≅ \operatorname{Spec}A$, and $f:X → Y$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use quasi-coherent modules $X.\mathrm{QCoh}$ on the small etale ringed site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], the equivalent small affine ringed model and its restriction $r_X$ [def-sfb-space-small-ringed-model], the canonical module direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] and its transported functor $F=f_*$ on small models [def-sfb-space-derived-module-calculus]. Let $G_X$ and $G_Y$ be the $A$-valued global-section functors [def-sfb-space-affine-global-sections], and $κ:G_X ≅ F ⋙ G_Y$ the chart-normalized ordinary section compositor [def-sfb-space-affine-sections-compositors]. For $q ∈ \mathbf N$ define functors $C_q(M)=R^q G_X(r_X M)$ and $D_q(M)=G_Y(R^q F(r_X M))$ on $X.\mathrm{QCoh}$, deriving in all module sheaves by injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For a nonnegative cochain complex $P$ of small-model modules define $C(P)=G_X(P)$ and $D(P)=F(P)$ termwise. For a family $e_q:C_q ≅ D_q$, define the affine higher-image section normalization by requiring, for every $q$, $M$ in $X.\mathrm{QCoh}$ and every injective resolution $I$ of $r_X M$, an $A$-linear map $c:G_Y(Z^q D(I)) → Z^q C(I)$ with
$$c ≫ i_C = G_Y(i_D) ≫ κ_{I^q}^{-1},$$
$$c ≫ π_C ≫ χ_{G_X,I,q}^{-1} ≫ e_{q,M} ≫ G_Y(χ_{F,I,q}) = G_Y(π_D).$$
Here $i$ is the cycles inclusion, $π$ is the cycles-to-cohomology projection, $χ_{H,I,q}:R^q H(r_X M) ≅ H^q(H(I))$ is the canonical injective-resolution comparison, and composition is in order of application. These are definitions of the two functors, the two complexes and the normalization predicate; no existence of a normalized family is asserted.
